claims.title: An unverified vendor-to-bucket transition could let an attacker borrow the master service's database write authority
claims.description: `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract` leaves the uncontrolled `boundary:vendor-platform` tenant and enters `boundary:cloud-account`, but its authentication is unknown. If the landing bucket does not authenticate and narrowly authorize this upload, a party able to act from the vendor side—or any caller accepted by the unresolved upload control—could place a chosen nightly extract in `store:landing-bucket`. `process:supplier-master-service` then loads that extract through `flow:supplier-master-service-to-landing-bucket:load-extract` and writes supplier records through `flow:supplier-master-service-to-supplier-database:write-supplier-records`; the attacker thereby causes the service to exercise its standing database-write authority. Second-order, this reaches supplier records in `store:supplier-database`, including the nightly supplier data and associated PII, rather than being limited to the landing bucket itself.

grounds.text: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account. Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unresolved authentication control on `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract`: the attacker needs access to the vendor-side upload path or an upload accepted without proper authorization, but the flow crosses from `boundary:vendor-platform` into `boundary:cloud-account`. Impact is high because the master service's downstream write reaches the supplier-record corpus in `store:supplier-database`, which holds PII and business-critical data.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and narrowly authorize vendor uploads to the landing bucket
mitigations.detail: Require a dedicated vendor workload identity on `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract`, grant it write access only to its designated prefix, and reject all other principals.

mitigations.summary: Prevent the loader from acting as an unchecked deputy
mitigations.detail: Have `process:supplier-master-service` accept only extracts with a verified vendor signature and expected schema, quarantine unexpected files, and constrain its database authority to the minimum supplier-record operations required.

claims.title: Password stuffing can impersonate suppliers in the portal
claims.description: An internet attacker can use credential-stuffing or phishing-obtained passwords to authenticate as `entity:supplier` on `flow:supplier-to-supplier-portal:upload-documents`, which uses a vendor-issued username and password. Because the flow crosses from the public internet to the internet-facing `process:supplier-portal`, a successful login gives the attacker a supplier session indistinguishable from the legitimate supplier's session, allowing them to upload paperwork as that supplier. Second-order: the portal writes uploaded documents to `store:document-store`, so the impersonation can place fraudulent compliance records alongside supplier PII and business-critical documentation.

grounds.text: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because `flow:supplier-to-supplier-portal:upload-documents` is a crossing from `boundary:public-internet` to the internet-facing `process:supplier-portal`, and password-only credentials are susceptible to commodity credential-stuffing and phishing. Impact is medium because the impersonated supplier can submit records through a flow carrying `pii` and `business-critical-data`, with the portal storing those documents in `store:document-store`.

mitigations.summary: Require phishing-resistant supplier authentication
mitigations.detail: Use WebAuthn/passkeys or another phishing-resistant MFA method for `flow:supplier-to-supplier-portal:upload-documents`, so a password alone cannot establish a supplier session.

mitigations.summary: Reduce password-reuse attacks
mitigations.detail: Screen passwords against known-breached-password sources and rate-limit and monitor authentication attempts to `process:supplier-portal`.

claims.title: Forged nightly extracts are possible if vendor push authentication is absent
claims.description: `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract` is an external-system-initiated boundary crossing from `boundary:vendor-platform` into `boundary:cloud-account`, and its `authentication` is unknown. If `store:landing-bucket` does not verify a vendor-specific sender identity, an attacker who can reach the upload endpoint could forge `entity:portal-vendor` and upload a fabricated nightly supplier extract. Second-order: `process:supplier-master-service` loads that extract through `flow:supplier-master-service-to-landing-bucket:load-extract` and writes supplier records to `store:supplier-database`, extending the forged vendor identity into the supplier system of record. This claim is conditional on resolving the unknown authentication attribute.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract:authentication`: the flow crosses from an external vendor platform, but the model does not establish whether the bucket verifies the sender. Impact is high because a forged full nightly extract carrying `pii` and `business-critical-data` is loaded by `process:supplier-master-service` and propagated into `store:supplier-database`.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate the vendor-to-bucket upload with a unique machine identity
mitigations.detail: Require a vendor-specific, least-privileged workload identity or mTLS client certificate for `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract`; do not infer vendor identity from endpoint reachability.

mitigations.summary: Verify extract provenance before loading
mitigations.detail: Require the vendor to sign each extract with a dedicated signing key and have `process:supplier-master-service` verify the signature, key identity, freshness, and replay protection before accepting the file.

claims.title: Nightly supplier extract can be modified in transit before import
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` remains unverified on the vendor-to-cloud boundary crossing `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract`, an on-path attacker can alter rows in the nightly supplier data extract before it reaches `store:landing-bucket`. `process:supplier-master-service` loads the extract from that bucket as-is through `flow:supplier-master-service-to-landing-bucket:load-extract` and writes resulting records through `flow:supplier-master-service-to-supplier-database:write-supplier-records`; therefore, forged supplier details or statuses can become authoritative records in `store:supplier-database`. This is conditional on the flow's unknown transport protection.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract:encryption_in_transit`: the attacker needs an on-path position across the vendor-platform-to-cloud-account crossing. Impact is high because the altered extract is loaded as-is into `store:supplier-database`, propagating corruption across supplier records carrying PII and business-critical data.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the vendor extract transfer
mitigations.detail: Require mutually authenticated TLS or an equivalent authenticated transfer protocol on `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract` and verify the negotiated transport configuration.

mitigations.summary: Verify extract integrity before loading
mitigations.detail: Require the vendor to sign each extract and have `process:supplier-master-service` verify the signature, signer identity, expected schema, and file hash before importing it.

claims.title: An unauthorized writer may plant a supplier extract for automated import
claims.description: If `authentication` is absent or insufficient on `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract`, an attacker able to reach the landing-bucket write interface can plant or replace the nightly supplier extract in `store:landing-bucket`. `process:supplier-master-service` retrieves that extract as-is through `flow:supplier-master-service-to-landing-bucket:load-extract` and writes its contents into `store:supplier-database`, laundering attacker-controlled supplier records into the authoritative database. This threat is conditional on the currently unknown caller authentication for the vendor write path.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:flow:portal-vendor-to-landing-bucket:push-nightly-extract:authentication`: exploitation depends on the unverified write authorization and access to the bucket interface. Impact is high because a planted file is consumed as-is by `process:supplier-master-service` and can corrupt the PII and business-critical supplier records in `store:supplier-database`.

mitigations.summary: Restrict landing-bucket writes to an identified vendor principal
mitigations.detail: Configure deny-by-default bucket policies and a dedicated, least-privilege vendor workload identity permitted only to write the expected extract object path.

mitigations.summary: Use immutable, verified imports
mitigations.detail: Enable versioning or write-once object retention for received extracts and require `process:supplier-master-service` to accept only signed, schema-validated files from the authorized vendor identity.

claims.title: Unbounded supplier document uploads can exhaust portal and document-storage capacity
claims.description: An authenticated but malicious supplier starting on `entity:supplier` can repeatedly submit oversized or computationally expensive compliance documents through `flow:supplier-to-supplier-portal:upload-documents` to `process:supplier-portal`. The crossing from `boundary:public-internet` makes the upload path externally reachable. If request-size, parse-complexity, per-supplier rate, and storage-quota limits are not enforced before the portal accepts documents, the attacker spends uploads while the vendor platform spends worker CPU, memory, bandwidth, and `store:document-store` capacity. Second-order, saturation of `process:supplier-portal` or its document storage prevents `entity:category-manager` from reviewing or recording approvals through `flow:category-manager-to-supplier-portal:review-documents`, and blocks legitimate supplier uploads; the supplier-document workflow is unavailable until capacity is recovered. This is conditional because the model does not state the relevant size, complexity, concurrency, or quota controls.

grounds.text: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `technology` on `process:supplier-portal`, `technology` on `store:document-store`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium: `flow:supplier-to-supplier-portal:upload-documents` crosses from `boundary:public-internet`, but exploitation requires a supplier-issued username and password; the portal and document-store technology and therefore their stated capacity controls are unknown. Impact is medium: `process:supplier-portal` supports supplier uploads and category-manager review, and `store:document-store` carries `pii` and `business-critical-data`; an exhaustion event disrupts the shared workflow but is recoverable.

mitigations.summary: Bound document work before allocation
mitigations.detail: At `process:supplier-portal`, enforce hard request and decompressed-document size limits, parser depth and expansion limits, content-type validation, and bounded/streaming document processing before storing the upload.

mitigations.summary: Apply supplier-specific quotas and load shedding
mitigations.detail: Set verified-identity rate, concurrency, and stored-byte quotas for `flow:supplier-to-supplier-portal:upload-documents`; reject excess uploads promptly rather than queueing work indefinitely.

mitigations.summary: Protect the shared review path from upload load
mitigations.detail: Use separate bounded worker and storage budgets for supplier uploads and category-manager review in `process:supplier-portal`, so upload saturation cannot starve approval and rejection activity.

The resulting approvals or rejections affect the business-critical supplier paperwork handled by `process:supplier-portal` and stored through `flow:supplier-portal-to-document-store:store-documents`.
